Timing of the analyses

Source: R/ms_looks.R
ms_looks.Rd

Defines when the interim and final analyses take place: when the expected number of events of an endpoint reaches given fractions of its final number of events, or at given calendar times, and which endpoints are tested at each analysis.

Usage

ms_looks(
  trigger = c("os", "pfs", "calendar"),
  fraction = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  test = NULL
)

Arguments

trigger

"os" or "pfs" for event-driven looks, or "calendar"; one value for all looks or one value per look.

fraction

Event fractions of the event-driven looks: with one trigger, strictly increasing and ending at 1 (defaults to 1, a single analysis); with one trigger per look, one value per look in (0, 1] (NA at calendar-driven looks).

time

Strictly increasing calendar times of the calendar-driven looks (with one trigger per look, one value per look, NA at event-driven looks).

test

NULL (all endpoints at all looks), or a list with one element per look giving the endpoints tested at the look ("os", "pfs" or both). A character vector with one endpoint per look is also accepted.

Value

An object of class ms_looks.

Details

With one value of trigger, all looks are driven by the events of the same endpoint ("os" or "pfs", with fraction) or take place at calendar times ("calendar", with time). The final number of events is given in ms_power through events or followup, and the look k takes place when the expected number of events of the trigger endpoint reaches fraction[k] times the final number.

With one value of trigger per look, each look has its own trigger. fraction then has one value per look, NA at the calendar-driven looks, and time one value per look, NA at the event-driven looks. The fractions of the looks driven by the events of an endpoint refer to the final number of events of that endpoint (see ms_power) and must be strictly increasing; an event-driven final look must have the fraction 1. The calendar times of the looks, which depend on the scenario, must be strictly increasing.

By default every look tests all endpoints of the test (ms_test). test gives the endpoints tested at each look, for example list("pfs", c("pfs", "os"), "os") for an interim analysis of PFS, the final analysis of PFS with an interim analysis of OS, and the final analysis of OS.

See also

ms_power, ms_size

Examples

ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 0.75, 1))
#> 3 look(s) driven by OS events at fractions: 0.50, 0.75, 1.00
ms_looks("calendar", time = c(24, 36))
#> 2 look(s) at calendar times: 24, 36
# PFS interim and final analyses driven by PFS events, an OS interim
# analysis at the final PFS analysis and the final OS analysis driven by
# OS events
ms_looks(c("pfs", "pfs", "os"), fraction = c(0.6, 1, 1),
         test = list("pfs", c("pfs", "os"), "os"))
#> 3 look(s):
#>   1: driven by PFS events at fraction 0.6; tests PFS
#>   2: driven by PFS events at fraction 1; tests PFS and OS
#>   3: driven by OS events at fraction 1; tests OS
